title: The Unofficial Locker
premise: Ines Marchetti, a cautious baker's son who kneads his unspoken feelings into bread, discovers a group chat called The Unofficial Locker that predicts events before they happen — and its latest prediction names him. To survive, he must win the school's meaningless baking championship and the district soccer final that secretly decides who the Locker's anonymous keeper spares. As Ines unravels the chat's origin, he finds it is powered by a classmate's stolen memories and a twenty-year-old injustice his own family buried. In the end, Ines wins neither trophy but exposes the Locker, choosing justice outside the law over survival, and bakes bread that finally tastes like truth.
about_author: Ulyana Amberdale grew up above her grandmother's bakery in a rust-belt town where everyone knew everyone's business, which taught her early how secrets rise like dough. She writes young adult stories about quiet kids forced into loud choices, and still judges people by what they order at 6 a.m.

chapters.title: Sourdough and Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. We meet him at 4 a.m. in Marchetti Bakery, kneading grief for his late mother into loaves no one can read. He's spent twenty years being careful: no risks, no feelings out loud, no soccer despite real talent. Beat: suffocating safety established.

chapters.title: The Message That Hadn't Happened Yet
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A stranger adds him to a dead group chat, 'The Unofficial Locker.' At 3:33 p.m. it posts tomorrow's fire drill — accurate to the minute — before the alarm sounds. Ines tells himself it's coincidence while his hands shake in the flour. Beat: dread arrives politely.

chapters.title: Second Prediction
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The chat predicts a bus crash that doesn't happen because Ines anonymously tips off the driver — proving he can change outcomes, and that the chat noticed. A reply appears: 'Intervention logged. Subject: I.M.' Beat: agency discovered, trap sprung.

chapters.title: The Keeper of the Roster
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. He narrows suspects among classmates: tech genius Priya, haunted transfer student Dov, and Coach Renner, who was at the school twenty years ago. Each interview scene doubles as a baking delivery. Beat: paranoia dressed as friendliness.

chapters.title: Bread That Tastes Like Lying
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. His father notices the loaves have gone bitter; customers complain. Ines realizes his baking mirrors his conscience. Meanwhile the chat posts a new rule: survive by winning two championships. Beat: the body keeps score.

chapters.title: Tryouts for a Game That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. He joins the soccer team after twenty years of avoidance, humiliating himself publicly. Only Dov defends him. The chat posts: 'Championship One: irrelevant. Championship Two: everything.' Beat: shame as entry fee.

chapters.title: Dov Remembers Wrong
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. We learn Dov's memories arrive in fragments that aren't all his own — including a night twenty years ago involving a locker, a fire, and a boy named Marco Marchetti. Beat: the past has a heartbeat.

chapters.title: Marco
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines confronts his father about Uncle Marco, erased from family photos: expelled after a locker-room fire he swore he didn't set, ruined by a vote of teammates. Dad goes silent. Beat: inheritance of a lie.

chapters.title: The Baking Championship Bracket
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Championship One begins: the school bake-off nobody cares about. Ines bakes honestly for the first time and advances, but the chat posts the full final bracket — before the semifinals are drawn. Beat: hope with a hook in it.

chapters.title: Priya's Firewall
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya admits she built the chat's interface but not its predictions; someone feeds it data through her old code. Together she and Ines trace the source to a server in the school basement. Beat: alliance forged in guilt.

chapters.title: What the Basement Keeps
chapters.summary: Ines and Priya's alternating POV. They find an old server wired to a wall of lockers, one sealed since the fire. Inside: Marco's confiscated journal. The predictions are generated from digitized pages of it. Beat: the Locker literally holds the past.

chapters.title: A Journal Written Backwards
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Marco's journal ends with a prophecy-like list — the chat isn't predicting the future; it's completing a revenge script Marco wrote before disappearing. Every 'prediction' is a step toward exposing the true arsonist. Beat: horror reframed as justice.

chapters.title: Coach Renner's Vote
chapters.summary: Renner's POV. Flashback interlude: twenty years ago, Renner, then a teammate, led the vote that expelled Marco to protect the real culprit — the beloved captain, now the town's mayor. Renner has been feeding the chat to force confession. Beat: complicity aging into cowardice.

chapters.title: Semifinal, Burnt Sugar
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Bake-off semifinal: Ines deliberately loses to protect a rival the chat threatened, breaking Championship One's 'win' condition. The chat responds coldly: 'Penalty accrued.' Beat: mercy has a price tag.

chapters.title: The Penalty
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Consequences cascade: his father's bakery lease is mysteriously challenged, Dov is suspended on fabricated grounds, and the chat offers one path to erase penalties — win the district final. Beat: the machine tightens.

chapters.title: Playing for Someone Else
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Training montage of the heart: Ines plays not to survive but to earn a stage big enough for the truth. Teammates who mocked him become allies when he shares Marco's story. Beat: a team forms around a wound.

chapters.title: The Mayor's Offer
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Mayor Calloway corners Ines: throw the final and the bakery is safe forever; expose the past and lose everything. He reveals the last prediction targets Dov. Beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, climactic match. Down two goals at halftime, Ines plays the game of his life — and wins the district final as the chat demanded. But from the podium he refuses the script: he reads Marco's journal aloud over the PA instead. Beat: victory weaponized into testimony.

chapters.title: The Unofficial Verdict
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The town erupts; no court will touch a twenty-year-old case, so the community convenes its own hearing in the gymnasium. Renner confesses fully; Calloway resigns under the weight of witnesses. Beat: justice outside the law, messy and human.

chapters.title: Shutting the Locker
chapters.summary: Priya and Ines's POV. They shut down the server and open the sealed locker, returning Marco's journal to a man found alive, estranged, working nights two towns over. The chat sends one final message: 'Case closed. Thank you, I.M.' Beat: release.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Careful
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Fallout: the bakery survives on new regulars, Dov returns, and Ines grieves the careful years he can't get back. His father finally says Marco's name out loud at the dinner table. Beat: accounting of cost.

chapters.title: The Bread That Tastes Like Him
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, closing. Ines bakes a loaf with no grief, no fear, no performance in it — just himself — and gives the first slice to Marco. The group chat stays silent forever. Final line: some championships don't matter, and that's how you know you won them. Beat: wholeness.
